definition: Self-interest means concern with, or pursuit of, one’s own benefit. In this historical source, it is the personal aim that individualism centers on, especially when regard for it becomes exclusive or excessive.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Individualism; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define “self-interest” as “concern with, or pursuit of, one’s own benefit”; it only describes “exclusive or excessive regard for self-interest.”
The definition’s first sentence therefore includes an unsupported characterization of what self-interest means beyond what the packet states.
The packet defines **individualism**, not **self-interest**; the requested sense is only indirectly related and not established as a headword sense in the source.

“Concern with, or pursuit of, one’s own benefit” is an unsupported paraphrase; the packet only says “exclusive or excessive regard for self-interest,” not that self-interest itself is defined as this.
“the personal aim that individualism centers on” goes beyond the source and introduces an unsupported framing about what individualism “centers on.”
